packages.name: Trigonometry Intuition
packages.tagline: See sine and cosine as coordinates on a circle, not memorized ratios.
packages.description: A community starter course demonstrating how a .syntaxcourse depends on a reusable .syntaxembeddedplugin (Unit Circle Lab) that installs automatically in one click.

customCourse.subtitle: Interactive coordinates on the unit circle

lessons.title: Cosine is Horizontal, Sine is Vertical
lessons.summary: Drag the Unit Circle Lab slider above to 0 deg, 90 deg, and 180 deg and watch the blue (x) and green (y) segments.
lessons.prompt: At 90 degrees (straight up on the unit circle), what are cos(90) and sin(90)?
lessons.explanation: At 90 degrees the point sits at (0, 1) on the unit circle, so horizontal cosine is 0 and vertical sine is 1.

lessons.title: Why 45 Degrees Makes Equal Legs
lessons.summary: Set the angle slider to 45 degrees. Notice that the right triangle inside the circle is isosceles.
lessons.prompt: At 45 degrees, how do cos(45) and sin(45) compare?
lessons.explanation: A 45-45-90 triangle has two equal legs, each equal to sqrt(2)/2, which is approximately 0.71.
